settings.title: AFFORDABLE Nil T2 Filing for Shelf Corporations

settings.editor:
A corporation that has never traded still owes returns, especially one incorporated years ago with no first transaction to point at. The obligation starts at incorporation rather than at first revenue, so a company registered in 2019 and never used owes seven returns. We file the whole run at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, with no surcharge for how far back it goes.

Whether the articles were filed to reserve a name, to hold an incorporation date ready for a bank or a tender, to carry a plan that changed, or because the company was bought ready-made, we file oldest first, attach Schedule 24 to the earliest return, and sign one T183CORP per year. You get the CRA confirmation for each.

settings.title: When a Shelf Corporation Stops Being Nil

settings.description_text: An account opened in the corporation name that earns any interest puts income in the year. The year is not nil.
One invoice ends the shelf period. From that tax year the corporation is trading and files an ordinary T2.
Property rolled into the corporation, often on a section 85 transfer, is a transaction with its own reporting.
The registration fee and legal costs are expenses. Claiming them makes that year active rather than nil.

settings.editor:
The usual complication is the incorporation year itself. Articles, name search and registry fees were paid by somebody, and where the corporation claimed them, its first year is an expense year with a loss rather than a nil year. Where the owner paid them personally and never put them through, the first year is nil like the rest.

A first year with costs in it is prepared by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca for $350.00 plus HST per year, and the remaining shelf years are filed here. Mixing the two in one catch-up is normal and the price applies year by year.

settings.title_text: Schedule 24 Goes on the Oldest Year
settings.description_text: Filing the recent years first and the oldest last puts Schedule 24 in the wrong return. Order matters here more than anywhere.

settings.title_text: Share Capital Is Still a Balance
settings.description_text: One share issued for one dollar is a balance sheet. That is usually what makes the GIFI schedules required.
Not at first revenue, and not at the date the owner meant to start. The registry date sets the first tax year.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • No invoice has ever been raised in the corporation name
  • No bank account was opened, or one was opened and never used
  • No asset was transferred into the corporation
  • Incorporation costs were paid personally and never claimed
  • No director or shareholder was paid anything

The year is not nil

  • A business account paid interest, however little
  • A first invoice was issued, even if it was never paid
  • Registration or legal costs were claimed by the corporation
  • Property was rolled in, on a section 85 transfer or otherwise
  • A government rebate or credit was received

Due either way

  • A T2 for every year since the incorporation date
  • Schedule 24 with the earliest outstanding return
  • Schedule 50 naming the subscriber who holds the shares
  • The annual return to the registry, which is not the T2
  • Dissolution, if the corporation is never going to be used

settings.title: How a Shelf Corporation Catches Up

settings.editor: Four steps from the filing form, however many years are outstanding.
A shelf corporation almost always runs the full sequence:
The registry date sets the first tax year and therefore how many returns are owed.
The fiscal year-end the Canada Revenue Agency holds has to match the return, or the transmission is rejected.
Oldest first, with Schedule 24 on the earliest and the GIFI schedules where share capital requires them.
One T183CORP per tax year. Each CRA confirmation is emailed within 3 business days.

settings.editor: Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, so six outstanding years is six times that and nothing else. The fee covers the T2, the GIFI schedules where required, Schedule 50, Schedule 24 on the first return, the T183CORP package with secure e-signing, CPA review before transmission, electronic transmission by a registered EFILE electronic filer, one corrected transmission where the Agency rejects the first, and the CRA confirmation emailed within 3 business days. A year in which the corporation started trading is $350.00 plus HST per year at gondaliyacpa.ca.

Shelf corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.

settings.title: Nil T2 Filing FAQs for Shelf Corporations

items.item_title: My corporation has never done anything. Do I owe returns?
How many years back do I have to go?
What is Schedule 24 and why does it matter here?
I never opened a bank account. Does that simplify it?
Who paid the incorporation fee changes things?
Can I just dissolve it and forget the returns?
Does an unused corporation still need an annual return?
What if I want to start using the corporation now?
Will the CRA have assessed it already?
Is a numbered corporation the same thing?

settings.editor: Yes, one for every tax year since the incorporation date. The obligation starts when the corporation comes into existence, not when it first earns anything.
All of them. An unfiled year does not expire, so a corporation incorporated in 2019 and never used owes every year from its first tax year to the most recent one.

It is the first-time filer schedule, and it goes with the first T2 after incorporation. For a shelf corporation that is the oldest outstanding year, which is why the returns are filed in order rather than newest first.
It helps. With no account there is no interest and no movement, which is the cleanest nil year there is. Share capital on the books may still put figures on the GIFI schedules.
It can. Where the corporation claimed the registration and legal costs, that year has expenses and is not nil. Where the owner paid personally and never charged them through, the year stays nil.
No. A clearance certificate will not be issued while a year is unfiled, and dissolution adds a final T2 due within six months. Filing first is what makes dissolution possible.
Yes, and it is a different filing from the T2. The federal annual return and the provincial equivalents are registry filings and are not included in this fee.
Then the shelf years are filed as nil and the year trading begins is an ordinary T2. Bringing the back years current first is what keeps the account clean.
It may have. A demand to file followed by an arbitrary assessment is common on long-unfiled corporations, and the real return is what replaces the figures the Agency invented.
Often, since many shelf corporations are never named. The number is the legal name and the return carries it exactly as the registry holds it.
